items.title: PPA Virginia Beach: rain pushes semis past 8 p.m.; 18-year-old Goins meets Martinez Vich in today's final
items.summary: Rain held up Saturday's play at the Mojo Energy Pouches Virginia Beach Open for about eight hours, per The Virginian-Pilot, so the singles and mixed doubles semifinals didn't start until after 8 p.m. ET. In men's singles, No. 5 John Lucian Goins (18, of Bradenton, Fla.) beat No. 2 Noe Khlif 13-11, 11-1 and will face No. 6 Jaume Martinez Vich, who beat No. 7 Adam Harvey 11-4, 11-6. In women's singles, top seed Kate Fahey reached the final on a walkover over No. 4 Chao Yi Wang. Her opponent is No. 21 Helena Jansen, who came back to beat No. 19 Sofia Sewing 12-14, 11-2, 11-9 for her first career semifinal win, per the PPA. The mixed final is Fahey/Eric Oncins (11-4, 11-6 over Daescu/Dizon) against Catherine Parenteau/Riley Newman (11-9, 4-11, 11-8 over Sleeth/Acevedo). Per the PPA, it's Parenteau/Newman's first mixed final together since 2024. The men's and women's doubles semifinals moved to 7 a.m. CT today. Finals start at 9 a.m. CT on PickleballTV, and Tennis Channel airs 9 a.m.-1 p.m. CT. All times depend on the weather.
items.social_angle: 'Teen vs. ex-tennis pro' final card: Goins (18) vs. Martinez Vich, plus Fahey's shot at a singles/mixed double. Post the CT times and update the DTP tournaments page right after the finals.

items.title: PPA Australia Pickleball Cup: Tardio and Black win two titles each; Alshon runner-up twice
items.summary: Gabe Tardio and Tyra Black each won two titles on Championship Sunday in Brisbane. Black/Tardio beat Parris Todd/Christian Alshon 7-11, 11-6, 11-7 in mixed. Tardio/Hayden Patriquin beat Tama Shimabukuro/JW Johnson 3-11, 11-6, 11-7 in men's doubles. Black/Jorja Johnson beat Todd/Danni-Elle Townsend 11-5, 11-6 in women's doubles. Hunter Johnson came back to beat Alshon 8-11, 11-5, 11-8 for the men's singles title, Alshon's second runner-up finish of the day. Australia's Andie Dikosavljevic, the No. 7 seed, beat Judit Castillo 11-6, 11-6 for the women's singles title. BayerRank's prediction model had given her a 4% title chance.
items.social_angle: Results carousel: 'Two titles each for Tardio and Black,' plus a 'Home hero' slide for Dikosavljevic (No. 7 seed, given a 4% title chance by BayerRank).

items.title: Franklin Malaysia apologizes after fans say ALW's Kuala Lumpur showcase was oversold
items.summary: Per the New Straits Times, Franklin Malaysia apologized to fans who went to the Anna Leigh Waters Asia Pro Showcase at 91 Pickleball, Hextar World @ Empire City in Kuala Lumpur. Fans had complained about overcrowding, long entry lines and too little seating, and some VIP package holders said they missed the merchandise and meet-and-greet they paid for, with some asking for full refunds. Franklin said: 'We acknowledge where we fell short, and we take responsibility for making things right.' It promised a dedicated channel for affected attendees but did not say when that channel would open or what the remedies would be. Meanwhile, a 'mother and daughter firefight' clip of Waters from the showcase is one of the top pickleball posts on Instagram today.
items.social_angle: Neutral fan-service explainer: 'Before you buy a pro meet-and-greet package: capacity, what's included, refund terms.' Don't pile on; Franklin has apologized.

items.title: APP Louisville: Livornese Jr./Munro win again; Stewart/Oshiro take their first gold as a pair
items.summary: At the Humana APP Louisville Open, Richard Livornese Jr. and Jack Munro beat Zack Marceau/Aidan Schenk 12-10, 11-2 for the men's pro doubles gold. The APP's preview said they came in with six straight men's pro doubles titles this season, which makes this seven. An APP social post put the streak at eight, so we are using the preview's count. Kat Stewart and Bobbi Oshiro won their first gold as a team, 11-2, 11-9 over Glauka Carvajal Lane/Domenika Turkovic. The bronzes went to Shelby Bates/Christine Maddox and Tanner Tomassi/Jay Devilliers. Earlier, No. 31 seeds Shay Hugo/Kevin Caufield upset the No. 2 seeds in the first round. Munro goes for another gold today in the mixed final with Roos Van Reek against Turkovic/Devilliers. The remaining bronze matches start at 10 a.m. CT. Also today: CBS Sports re-airs the APP Columbus Open at 3 p.m. CT.

sources.label: APPTV (YouTube, Van Reek/Munro to the final)

items.title: The Picklr bankruptcy: first-day court hearing set for Monday at 1:30 p.m. CT
items.summary: A notice filed Oct. 16 in The Picklr's Chapter 11 (Subchapter V) case sets an emergency first-day hearing for Monday, Oct. 19 at 1:30 p.m. CT. It will be held by Webex before Judge Scott W. Everett of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Texas in Dallas. The court will take up five requests: jointly administering the Picklr, Inc. and Picklr Clubs Inc. cases, interim postpetition (DIP) financing, keeping the current cash-management system, paying prepetition wages and benefits, and getting more time to file schedules and financial statements. Business Journals coverage continued Saturday, repeating the roughly $19M in total liabilities first reported by SBJ.
items.social_angle: Short 'What happens Monday in the Picklr case' explainer, with a promised follow-up after the hearing. Stick to the filings and don't speculate about closures.

items.title: Next up: PPA Tour Asia's Hong Kong Slam (Oct. 19-25), where seven players can complete the 'dragon' medal set
items.summary: The Hang Seng Bank Hong Kong Slam (PPA Asia 1500) at Kai Tak Arena closes out the 2026 PPA Tour Asia season. This year, each medal is a piece of a 'dragon' set, and the head is only awarded in Hong Kong. Seven players arrive with the other two pieces and can complete the set by reaching a final: Tama Shimabukuro, Alix Truong, Sahra Dennehy, Danni-Elle Townsend, Hien Truong, Len Yang and Joey Wild. Shimabukuro (15) and Alix Truong could win an all-gold 'golden dragon' with a title. Christopher Haworth makes his Asia debut in mixed with Alix Truong, and Federico Staksrud teams with Townsend in mixed.
items.social_angle: 'Chase the Dragon' explainer graphic: who needs what in Hong Kong. Good cross-promo while the U.S. tour heads into Worlds.

items.title: PicklePod clips: compassion vs. competition, 'guess the DUPR,' and why only about 1% of rated players are 5.0+
items.summary: The Dink is pushing clips from its latest PicklePod, in which Zane Navratil and Nico (@NicoTheLefty) debate whether compassion has a place in pro pickleball, play 'guess the DUPR' from highlights, and compare 5.0 ratings across cities. The '1% are 5.0' line comes from DUPR data The Dink published Oct. 7. About 1% of global DUPR doubles players with a result in the past 12 months are rated 5.0 or higher, about 5% are 4.5+, about 16% are 4.0+, and the most common range is 3.0-3.499 (29%). The snapshot is as of Sept. 22.

items.title: PPA Virginia Beach Open: No. 1 seeds fall on the way to Semifinal Saturday
items.summary: Jaume Martinez Vich beat No. 1 seed Roscoe Bellamy 11-2, 11-7 to reach his first singles semifinal since 2025. No. 8 Max Freeman and Jonathan Truong took out No. 1 Klinger/Oncins 2-11, 11-6, 11-6, Layne Sleeth and Nico Acevedo upset No. 1 Pisnik/Khlif in mixed, and Sofia Sewing is into her first career PPA women's singles semifinal. Earlier in the week, Estee Widdershoven beat Genie Bouchard 11-5, 13-11 and Chao Yi Wang ended Maria Ford's run in the quarterfinals. The women's singles semifinalists are Kate Fahey, Chao Yi Wang, Sofia Sewing and Helena Jansen. In men's singles, PickleFitter lists Martinez Vich vs. Adam Harvey and Noe Khlif vs. John Lucian Goins. Semis air today on PickleballTV (11 a.m.-7 p.m. CT) and Tennis Channel (11 a.m.-2 p.m. CT), weather permitting.

items.title: Lea Jansen is playing on a broken patella; out about 3 months and has withdrawn from all remaining 2026 events
items.summary: Pickleball.com reports that Jansen withdrew from singles and mixed at Virginia Beach because of a broken patella in her left leg, but kept playing women's doubles with Kate Fahey. According to The Dink's Erik Tice, she had played on the injured leg since May during the MLP season. She expects to miss about three months and has pulled out of every event for the rest of 2026. Fahey/Jansen then lost 11-7, 11-6 to Alix Truong/Layne Sleeth (per Dinks & Volleys). Jansen said 'there are a lot of things unknown in my career right now' and 'if this is the last time I go out, I'd like to do it with Kate.' She has not announced a retirement.
items.social_angle: Respectful 'Get well, Lea' post featuring her quote. Do NOT frame it as a retirement.

items.title: The Picklr bankruptcy: local fallout and new filing details
items.summary: Business Journals in Houston, Orlando, Seattle and Philadelphia, plus AL.com, the Daily Press and MONTCO.Today, ran local angles in the past day. Houston's angle is that the chain filed halfway through its expansion plans there. Per IAPPF, the parent entity's Aug. 31 balance sheet in the petition shows about $915K in assets, $2.39M in liabilities and seven disputed, contingent guaranty claims of about $783K. SBJ separately reported about $19M in total liabilities as of March, taken from the franchise disclosure document. A debtors' motion asks the court to push the deadline for filing schedules to Nov. 6. The Dink's PicklePod says courts are 'becoming commoditized' and the facility boom could face a 'reality check.' UNCONFIRMED: IAPPF cites unnamed sources who say the lease guarantees total in the millions.
items.social_angle: Follow-up explainer: 'What the Picklr filing actually says.' Petition numbers vs. the $19M figure, in plain terms. Keep the 'millions in guarantees' line labeled unconfirmed.

items.title: PPA Australia Pickleball Cup: Alshon reaches two finals as his social media manager's run ends
items.summary: In Brisbane, Christian Alshon beat Tama Shimabukuro 11-4, 11-2 to reach the men's singles final, where he meets Hunter Johnson (11-9, 11-3 over Grayson Goldin). Alshon and Parris Todd also reached the mixed final with an 11-8, 11-9 win over Irvine/Patriquin. Gabe Tardio is in two finals: men's doubles with Hayden Patriquin and mixed with Black. Shimabukuro/JW Johnson made the men's doubles final, and Judit Castillo meets Andie Dikosavljevic for the women's singles title. Earlier, Benjamin Bramblett, Alshon's hitting partner and social media manager, filled in after Federico Staksrud's visa issues and reached the men's doubles quarterfinals with him; they lost there to Wall/Wild 11-6, 11-7.
items.social_angle: Feel-good story: 'From the social media desk to the PPA quarterfinals.' Bramblett's run makes a great carousel.

items.title: Worlds countdown: MLP Nations Cup promo push; Mark Wahlberg to headline celebrity showdown

items.title: Selkirk launches the S2 Pro ball with a 1-year no-crack warranty
items.summary: Selkirk published its S2 Pro introduction on Oct. 16. The ball has a patented 38-hole geodesic design with three hole sizes and a textured surface, plus what Selkirk calls an industry-first 1-Year No-Crack, Out-of-Round Warranty. It is the official ball of the APP Asia Tour. Selkirk's post also lays out the pro ball landscape: Life Time's LT Pro 48 is the official ball of the PPA and MLP, and the Franklin X-40 is the official ball of the APP U.S. Tour. Selkirk is running an Instagram giveaway (entries close 10/19).

items.title: The Picklr files Chapter 11
items.summary: Indoor franchisor The Picklr filed for Chapter 11 late Oct. 9 to renegotiate lease guarantees on about 40 franchise locations, with $4.8M in DIP financing from Tom Neale's Dynamus Alliance. The CEO says no clubs close as a direct result, but he expects the company to shrink.

items.title: Club boom meets shakeout: 6 chains grew 145 -> 199 locations
items.summary: The Dink, using Business of Pickleball data, reports six franchise chains grew from 145 to 199 locations between January and September, but September added only 70 net indoor courts (418 were added in June). Ace, Pickleball Kingdom and PickleRage all grew sharply.
